phrase.zh: 细小的颗粒，也有自己的世界。
phrase.en: Tiny particles have worlds of their own.

visual.zh: 厚壁淡青玻璃容器占据右侧，内盛深红液体，旁边立着带窄缝的小黄铜块，左下散落三粒金色圆珠。黑白版保留物件、大小关系与裁切，刻纹更明显。画面借观察小颗粒的研究构成原创寓意，圆珠数量不是实验数据。
visual.en: A thick pale teal glass cell fills the right with deep red liquid, beside a small slit brass block; three tiny gold beads lie at lower left. Monochrome retains the objects, scale and crop with stronger hatching. This is an original metaphor for observing particles; bead count is not experimental data.

background.zh:
齐格蒙迪独获1925年诺贝尔化学奖，奖项于1926年颁发。他研究胶体——微小颗粒分散在液体中的体系，并与合作伙伴发展超显微镜，借颗粒散射的光观察它们。红色液体与玻璃容器是这项研究的原创寓意，不是实际装置复原、颗粒大小或数量数据。短句为原创。
1925年化学奖；独享本年度奖项。获奖理由（中文译述）：表彰他揭示胶体溶液的不均一性质，以及由此建立的胶体研究方法。
background.en:
Zsigmondy received the entire 1925 Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1926 for colloid research and its methods. Colloids contain tiny particles dispersed in a liquid. He developed an ultramicroscope with collaborators to observe light scattered by particles. The red liquid and glass cell are an original metaphor, not an apparatus reconstruction or particle-size/count data. The phrase is original.
1925 — The Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Received the full prize. Official motivation: for his demonstration of the heterogenous nature of colloid solutions and for the methods he used, which have since become fundamental in modern colloid chemistry
